marketEvents.visionText: The invaders will open their largest land offensive in a generation; tank columns will roll east.
marketEvents.headlineText: Fire Nation opens three fronts in the west; tank columns advance singing. The Fire Lord calls it 'a good start.'

affectedCompanies.explanation: Three fronts of tank columns are three fronts of replacement hulls. The market bought the war machine at full price — then spent the season paying for it.
Every steamship and boiler behind the offensive burns its coal. The 'safer' way to be long the war — until the war stopped.

marketEvents.visionText: The invaders' navy will blockade the southern sea lanes; merchant ships will be boarded or turned back.
marketEvents.headlineText: Fire Navy blockades the southern lanes. Boardings, seizures, forced turnarounds; sea prunes declared contraband.

affectedCompanies.explanation: Its whole business is the thing the blockade closed. The cast sheet said so: every route a sea lane.
A blockade cannot board a hawk. Scrolls that sailed yesterday flew today, at hawk rates — first leg of the season's quietest compounder.

marketEvents.visionText: Families burned out of the west will triple the crowds seeking passage to the walled capital.
marketEvents.headlineText: Refugee arrivals at Ba Sing Se triple in four days; ferries add night crossings. The ticket queue has its own queue.

affectedCompanies.explanation: The only paid passage into the walled capital, oversold three times over. The identity was easy; the catch came later.
A displaced family's first purchase is the cheapest food in the square. For one glorious month, Cabbage Corp compounded.

marketEvents.visionText: Quartermasters of both armies will bid against each other for every barrel of blasting jelly on the market.
marketEvents.headlineText: Blasting-jelly prices triple as both armies bid on the same barrels; the Yu Dao works add a third shift and a fence.

affectedCompanies.explanation: TRAP, part one: the bidding war was real, but the tape priced its peak as permanent. Chasers were still holding when the Earth King answered.

marketEvents.visionText: The mountain city, second stronghold of the Earth Kingdom, will open its gates without a siege.
marketEvents.headlineText: Omashu surrenders without a siege; its new governor renames it New Ozai. Civilians get two days and one cart each.

affectedCompanies.explanation: One network, one city, one bad morning. The cast sheet had warned exactly this.
Omashu's evacuees had two days and one destination. Refugee leg two.
An occupied city's mail doesn't stop — it reroutes, by wing, at rush rates. Quiet leg two.

marketEvents.visionText: A runaway tank will roll driverless through a market square and come to rest on a famous produce cart.
marketEvents.headlineText: A driverless tank rolls through Gaoling's market and stops atop Cabbage Corp's flagship cart. Proprietor: 'MY CABBAGES!'

affectedCompanies.explanation: The tank found the flagship cart, as somehow it always does. Net of the refugee windfall: flat on the season. That is the joke.

marketEvents.visionText: A siege engine the size of a village will crawl toward the walled capital, and the city will bar its gates.
marketEvents.headlineText: A drill two hundred paces long grinds toward the outer wall; gates sealed. Officials: 'There is no war in Ba Sing Se.'

affectedCompanies.explanation: Nobody queues for ginseng while a drill chews the wall. Siege panic marked down the whole upper ring.
Barred gates, suspended crossings, suspended revenue — the refugee trade's first lesson in what it was exposed to.
'Siege engines' had been on the cast sheet all season. The drill was Sozin's flagship build, paid for in advance of the wall it hadn't broken.

marketEvents.visionText: The great siege engine will die at the wall it has bitten into, and the capital's gates will reopen.
marketEvents.headlineText: The drill bites through the outer wall, then splits open from within; a boy stands atop the wreck. Gates reopen.

affectedCompanies.explanation: The wall held, but took a bite doing it — and one company holds the standing repair contract. No vision ever said 'quarry.'
Relief rally: gates open, panic over, nobles back in their seats by evening.
Crossings resumed into a city the continent now believes unbreakable. Leg three of four.
Its terror weapon died in public, opened by one boy. The invincibility premium came off in an afternoon.

marketEvents.visionText: When the moon swallows the sun, a fleet will strike the invaders' capital; no firebender will hold a flame.
marketEvents.headlineText: Eclipse invasion hits the Fire Nation capital; palace holds, foundry ring burns. Firebenders report: no fire.

affectedCompanies.explanation: The cut the season was built on, drawn on the sheet in advance: firebender smelters, foundry ringing the capital. Eight minutes without fire and half the order book had nowhere to be forged. The obvious coal hedge failed — Caldera runs machines, far away.
Three continents paying rush rates for dispatches in the chaos. Quiet leg three, still unnamed.

marketEvents.visionText: The Earth King will requisition every barrel of blasting jelly in his realm at a price fixed by his generals.
marketEvents.headlineText: Royal decree: all blasting jelly requisitioned at fixed prices. Yu Dao cancels the third shift, then the fence.

affectedCompanies.explanation: TRAP, part two: requisition at a general's idea of fair. Round trip complete, net zero — the market pays for scarcity, not drama.

marketEvents.visionText: The Avatar, gone a hundred years, will be proclaimed returned; truce envoys will sail for every capital.
marketEvents.headlineText: Earth King proclaims the Avatar returned — the boy from the drill. Truce envoys sail; the Fire Lord will receive them.

affectedCompanies.explanation: Armistice talk cancels the order book's premise. Final leg of the round trip: up seventeen on the offensive, down twenty-one by the close.
The navy that burns its coal sailed home. Did everything right all season; flattened by peace.
Truce banners lift the blockade — the season's last relief rally, not enough to reach shore.
The counter-intuitive close: peace is wonderful for everyone but a ferry priced on endless exodus.
The capital exhaled and ordered tea. A retired general does his best business in peacetime.

debrief.summary: The market did the obvious thing: it bought the war machine. That was the season's most expensive idea. Sozin Steelworks rode the offensive and its own drill, then gave it all back — humiliated at the wall, burned out by an eclipse its own cast-sheet line foretold, marked down by the first whisper of peace. The money went to the toll-takers beside the war: Talon Post, named by no vision, compounded three quiet legs — a blockade its hawks flew over, an occupied city's rerouted mail, an invasion's dispatch traffic — into the cleanest win on the board, and Badgermole Quarries collected the repair commission of the century for a wall that held. The traps closed on schedule: Yu Dao's bidding war ended in requisition for a net of nothing, and Caldera Coalworks, the 'safe' way to be long the war, was flattened by the armistice that ended it. Omashu Chute & Parcel was the concentration lesson — one network, one city, one bad morning. The ferries and the tea house round-tripped the siege and came out ahead, though peace clipped the ferry's exodus premium at the close. Kyoshi Island Charters and White Lotus Imports never printed a line: neutrality and back rooms are quiet businesses. And Cabbage Corp? Up on refugee appetites, down one flagship cart, flat on the season. He will rebuild.
